chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Umar al-Sayqal, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Sakuni, from Ali ibn Ismail al-Maysami, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send a Prophet except with a beautiful voice.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of a beautiful voice in Prophets according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in al-Kafi’s chapter on Quranic recitation, establishes that a melodious voice is an innate divine attribute of all Prophets, serving as a spiritual sign of their truthfulness. In Shia scholarship, this is often linked to the concept of *Jamal al-Tajwid* (beauty of recitation), where the Prophet Muhammad’s voice is seen as the ultimate manifestation of this trait, enhancing the emotional and spiritual impact of the Quran on the listener. It underscores that the aesthetic quality of recitation is not merely artistic but a sacred characteristic inherited from the divine source.
